evidence.finding: Formal 12-case geo_mean 0.9625098543. Largest cases (4096x4096, 16777216 elems) speedup: fp16 0.614 (27.84us vs 17.10us), bf16 0.636 (29.92 vs 19.03), fp32 0.933 (30.97 vs 28.91). All <=1M-element cases are ~0.98-1.16, so launch/hot-path overhead is already at parity. exp(-sum(log_loss)/12)=exp(-0.4586/12)=0.9625 reproduces the geo_mean; the two 16-bit large cases alone contribute 0.9403 of the 0.4586 loss sum.

Candidate fp16-large / fp32-large = 27.84/30.97 = 0.90, but reference fp16-large / fp32-large = 17.10/28.91 = 0.59. The reference gains ~41% by halving bytes (bandwidth-bound) while the candidate gains only ~10%, so the 16-bit path is not bandwidth-bound: extra per-element fp32-promotion vector work dominates the large 16-bit calls. Small cases at parity confirm the gap is device arithmetic, not host launch.

Both Triton kernels compute y = (x.to(tl.float32) * 57.29577951308232).to(x.dtype). For float16/bfloat16 this materializes a full fp32 tile and adds two full-tile type-conversion vector ops (16-bit->fp32 and fp32->16-bit) that the fp32 path does not have; it also introduces a second rounding relative to a single native-dtype multiply.

Prior pointwise candidate 8600ce070318 that only changed the math dtype passed the same formal contract >0.8, i.e. dtype-selective arithmetic is an accepted, correctness-preserving lever here. The launch-path/cached-launcher work is already present in this candidate (small cases ~1.0).

No actual_ir, no paired_evidence, no roofline, no simulator, no runtime_api excerpt (host_diagnosis/compiler_comparison null). Therefore no instruction-level or bandwidth claim is asserted; the mechanism is inferred only from per-dtype per-case walltime ratios.

hypothesis: The 16-bit gap is caused by promoting the whole tile to fp32 for the single scale multiply. The native-dtype CANN reference performs the multiply in the input dtype; doing the same removes two full-tile conversion vector ops, making the fp16/bf16 large calls bandwidth-bound and close to the reference. float32 arithmetic is numerically unchanged (a single fp32 multiply either way).
change: In both Triton kernels replace (x.to(tl.float32) * 57.29577951308232).to(x.dtype) with x * tl.full((1,), 57.29577951308232, x.dtype), forcing the multiply to run in the input dtype (native fp16/bf16; identical fp32). Launcher ABI, cache keys, alignment/device/stream guards, strided index decomposition, tail mask and exactly-once cold path are all left unchanged.
expected: 4096x4096 fp16 and bf16 candidate_us should drop toward the reference (roughly 17-19us) with speedups moving from 0.61/0.64 toward ~0.9-1.0; fp32 and all <=1M cases unchanged; geo_mean should rise from 0.9625 toward/over 1.0 (parity on both 16-bit large cases alone gives exp(0.4817/12)=1.041). Correctness: max relative deviation ~8e-4 (fp16) / ~6e-3 (bf16), within the tolerance that already accepts the native CANN reference.
validation: Tool-bridge preflight, then full KGS 36/36 plus both 42/42 supplementary checks; compare per-case speedups against the 0.9625098543 starting measurement. If any correctness case fails, revert the kernels to fp32 promotion and record the regression.
